gaps.sentence: By Friday, the court ___ its verdict.
gaps.explanation: 'By Friday' — future perfect for completion before a future moment.

gaps.sentence: I ___ that film three times, and I would happily watch it again.
gaps.hint: life experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Experience up to the present with no specific past time takes the present perfect: have seen.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather ___ walk five miles to school when he was a boy.
gaps.hint: a past habit no longer true
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' describes past habits or states that are no longer true: used to walk.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three novels since she retired.
gaps.explanation: 'Since she retired' (up to now) — present perfect.

gaps.sentence: Every morning she ___ an hour in the garden before breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' marks a repeated routine, which takes the present simple: spends.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.
